claim: Build::promote must stop silently overwriting a committed ref, republishRef must make destination re-drives idempotent, and Build::abandon must retire build_seq only after precommit removal.
A different committed manifest at the destination of Build::promote is a reachable durable conflict and must be refused with ErrorCodes::ABORTED, not LOGICAL_ERROR.
republishRef is idempotent when the destination is already committed with the same content; a different-content destination is an ABORTED conflict.
Build::abandon retires build_seq after its precommit-removal CAS, while alive is set false early.
The TLA+ model's RefFreeFor guard permits a ref to own at most one committed manifest, so the C++ promote guard is a model-alignment requirement.
The promote regression tests use inline manifest entries with distinct inline bytes so they exercise manifest conflicts without requiring real blob objects.
A same-manifest re-promote is allowed and must be idempotent; the guard compares the existing manifest_ref with the manifest_ref being promoted rather than rejecting every already-committed ref.
republishRef compares only the source and destination PartManifest entries and drops the source ref without staging a new manifest when the entries match.
republishRef must not drop the source when the destination is committed to different content; it throws ErrorCodes::ABORTED instead.
After the precommit-removal mutation is durably committed, Build::abandon retires build_seq; the staged-manifest debris cleanup remains best-effort afterward.

Build::promote unconditionally overwriting root.refs[final_ref_name] can leave the old Committed binding in the journal without its releasing -1 owner event, pinning the old manifest and uniquely owned blobs.
Promoting over a pre-existing committed ref can leave two live Committed bindings for one ref and later make dropRef remove only the new binding, creating owner↔refs divergence.

PROMOTE-OVER-COMMITTED-LEAK is a liveness and space leak rather than a dangling-reference or data-loss violation; INV_NO_DANGLE, INV_NO_LOSS, and INV_COMMIT_FAILCLOSED still hold in the described failure.

republishRef can reach the overwrite leak when a crash or exception occurs after promote(dst) and before dropRef(src), because its source-only idempotency gate then re-stages a fresh ManifestId on retry.
ABANDON-RETIRE-ORDERING allows GC to see a watermark-dead but not-yet-removed precommit and append a duplicate removal while abandon appends its own removal.

The combined fix is fail-close promote, idempotent republishRef re-drive, and retire-after-removal abandon; reachable refusal cases use ABORTED because LOGICAL_ERROR is reserved for impossible invariants.
Build::promote proceeds when the target ref is absent or already names the same manifest_ref, and throws ABORTED when it names a different committed manifest_ref.

A different-content overwrite is not treated as a legitimate repoint because MergeTree parts are immutable and mutations mint new names; the intended republish path handles re-drive conflicts explicitly.
republishRef determines idempotency from PartManifest::entries, not ManifestId, because a re-drive mints a new manifest ID for the same content.
PartManifest::entries are canonical path-sorted vectors, so element-wise vector equality is stable for comparing source and destination content.
Comparing whole PartManifest objects is rejected because ref, root_namespace_id, and payload_digest legitimately differ between source and destination manifests.
When the destination ref is absent, republishRef retains the normal stageManifest → precommitAdd → promote → dropRef sequence.
Moving retireBuildSeq after precommit removal makes the precommit watermark-dead only after removal is durably committed, closing the double-removal window.
The combined changes preserve INV_NO_DANGLE and INV_NO_LOSS; a different-content republish conflict fails closed without silently losing the source content.
A cache disk over a content-addressed disk originally failed at startup because MetadataStorageFromCacheObjectStorage did not forward isContentAddressed or the content-addressed transaction surface.
The cache-over-content-addressed fix reuses the content-addressed metadata storage directly and wraps only the object storage layer.
The CA integration harness uses RustFS rather than MinIO because the CAS tests require conditional-PUT semantics that MinIO did not enforce in the observed setup.
A cache over CA eliminated repeated remote reads in the probe: warmed cached CA reached about 45 ms with zero S3 GETs versus about 141 ms and 186 GETs for raw CA.
The cache disk and policy remain opt-in because cache population and cache-mediated writes slow cold or single-pass workloads even though warm repeated reads benefit.
The validated CAS safety core is one key per hash plus an in-body incarnation_tag and exact-token body deletion; the freshness-meta work left that core unchanged.

The tokened promote-condemn race was caused by GC condemning freshly put blobs before the precommit-to-blob edge had been folded, and the tokened fix re-uploaded from retained writer sources after the owner check.
The tokenless promote-condemn race occurred when the pre-refresh copy-forward pre-pass missed a condemnation revealed by the in-closure refresh; an in-closure copy-forward backstop closed that gap.
The EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE conclusion is that publishStaging orders stageManifest → precommitAdd → putBlob → promote, so every blob observation occurs after a durable protecting edge.
The dedup-adoption condemnation check remains safety-critical because adoption does not mutate the existing incarnation and a graduated delete can race an adoption that was not checked.

The raw-body and terminal-tombstone variants were rejected because removing the in-body incarnation tag makes the body etag content-derived and prevents exact-token deletion from missing a resurrected body.
Per-incarnation blob keys were rejected because they require a 404-to-LIST generation-resolution path, propagate incarnation into manifests, and need additional floors or pins.
The freshness-meta v3 direction keeps the in-body tag and uses per-hash metadata only as a writer freshness point-read, not as the delete linearizer.

A GC liveness wedge was traced to a condemn-race retry that republished the same ManifestIds while mf_cleanup retained removal-half entries, allowing a later removal fold to delete live bodies and clamp collection on missing bodies.
The GC-wedge fix was validated by a 20-minute chaos run with dangling=0, no removal-fold clamps, and subsequent clean fsck with unreachable=0 and pending_gc=0.

The post-mortem method for a torn-down CA pool is to run RustFS over the surviving data directory and open it with clickhouse-local in readonly mode so owner-claim, mount-lease, and GC mutations are skipped.
The CA-s3 timeout investigation found stalled queries were bound to public web-disk HTTP reads, with zero CA/RustFS wait, so those timeouts were not caused by the CA changes.
A tokened blob condemned between putBlob and promote must be resurrected from the writer's own source so an ordinary CA-over-S3 INSERT succeeds without exposing a retryable ABORTED to the client.
Build retains a parallel map of BlobSource objects for every putBlob hash, including streamed uploads and dedup-adopted blobs, because DepEntry is reassigned on adopt paths.
BlobSource retains a size and a closure that rereads a pending-blob temporary file; it does not retain the payload in memory, and the temporary file remains until commit cleanup after promote.
Tokened resurrection runs only after the promote owner-liveness check, so an abandoned build aborts without producing an orphan incarnation.
The tokened promote revalidation uses a bounded loop of up to eight attempts, re-HEADing after each source upload and failing with ABORTED if the leaf remains absent or condemned.
uploadFromSource re-uploads the writer's bytes through head, putIfAbsentStream, and putOverwrite without backend().get, preserving INV-1.
Accepting a condemned token without resurrecting it is unsound because exact-token GC deletion can graduate and delete that incarnation, leaving the committed manifest dangling.

A synchronous writer-triggerable fold barrier that activates the precommit edge before revalidation is the ideal zero-reupload fix, but it is out of scope because no production writer↔GC fold API exists.
With gc_interval_sec=5, GC can condemn a freshly written blob in the putBlob→promote window and cause ordinary INSERT to fail with ABORTED at promote's blob revalidation.
The write path is stageManifest → precommitAdd → putBlob → promote, and the precommit-to-blob edge protects a new blob only after GC folds the create-precommit event with the manifest body.

Build::promote's prior fail-closed revalidation aborted on a condemned tokened leaf even though that leaf had a retained writer source; the existing copy-forward pre-pass intentionally handled only tokenless adoptEvidence leaves.
The tokened fix retains BlobSource in a parallel map for every putBlob hash, including dedup-adopted hashes, because later condemnation can affect an adopted incarnation too.
Resurrection is placed after owner-liveness validation rather than in the pre-pass because the build's precommit is the tokened blob's only protection.
A source-backed condemned or absent blob is re-uploaded and rechecked in a bounded loop; a tokened dependency without a retained source remains an ABORTED fail-closed backstop.
The tokenless copy-forward GET remains the sole documented exception to the never-read-the-dying-object rule; tokened resurrection uses uploadFromSource instead.
Eight re-condemnations within one promote closure are considered unreachable at a five-second GC interval, making the bounded loop effectively deterministic while remaining honestly bounded.

The tokenless promote backstop applies to present-condemned tokenless adoptEvidence leaves revealed after the in-closure refresh; absent tokenless leaves and unknown leaves still fail closed with ABORTED.
Build::promote keeps the outside-the-lock tokenless copy-forward pre-pass as a fast path and adds an in-closure backstop for condemnations visible only in the refreshed view.
isCopyForwardableTokenless is true only for a Blob dependency with no token, representing adoptEvidence with an independent committed owner; tokened or missing dependencies are not copy-forwardable.
The in-closure condemned branch chooses uploadFromSource for a tokened source, copyForwardFromCondemned for a copy-forwardable tokenless dependency, and ABORTED otherwise.
The absent branch remains unchanged because copyForwardFromCondemned requires a present object to GET and cannot recreate an absent tokenless blob.
The backstop runs after the in-closure refresh and owner-liveness check, preventing consequential copy-forward work on an aborting path.
The tokenless race exists because the pre-pass observes retire-view round R while mutateShard may refresh the view to R′, making condemnations in (R,R′] visible only to the in-closure revalidation.
copyForwardFromCondemned verifies the condemned payload hash against the content key and republishes a fresh incarnation using token-conditional putOverwrite.
The in-closure backstop is mandatory even if the pre-pass is refreshed opportunistically, because GC may advance again before the closure's fence-round refresh.
The copy-forward backstop is idempotent under CAS retry and terminates because a successful copy-forward produces a fresh token absent from the fixed in-closure snapshot.

The production publish order stageManifest → precommitAdd → putBlob → promote is the EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE protocol: every blob observation occurs under a durable closure edge naming the manifest's hashes.
A durable precommit closure cannot be deleted by GC once a per-shard seal after precommitAdd folds the closure edge, because d becomes at least one and the entry is spared.
The per-shard seal is taken when the target shard is read, not once globally for the whole GC pass; the edge theorem still holds because the closure is stored in that target shard's journal.
A blob condemned after precommitAdd is doomed to be spared at the next fold, while a blob already graduated before precommitAdd must be detected by the writer and displaced with a fresh incarnation.
The K1 dedup-adoption gate is safety-critical: adopting an existing incarnation is invisible to GC's in-flight delete decision, so a condemned adopted blob must be displaced with a fresh incarnation.
The settled v3 blob layout keeps one key per hash and a minimal in-body 16-byte incarnation_tag plus payload; the manifest remains pure content and reads use a constant offset.
GC deletes blob bodies with DELETE If-Match against the condemn-time body token; resurrecting with a fresh in-body tag changes the etag so the old exact-token delete misses.
The per-hash .meta object is a two-state clean/condemned freshness marker with condemn_round and size; it is not the delete linearizer and is not read by the data path.
The v3 meta key is blobs/xx/<hash>.meta, while the body remains blobs/xx/<hash>; GC writes condemned before deletion, clears it on spare, and deletes it after the body.
A strongly consistent meta GET is a pool requirement because the writer must not adopt a body whose current incarnation has already been condemned.
Fresh upload writes the body before a clean meta; dedup adoption point-reads the meta and adopts clean or absent metadata, while condemned metadata triggers resurrection.

Tokenless copy-forward reads a still-present condemned body only for an adoptEvidence dependency with an independent committed source owner, verifies the payload hash, and republishes a fresh incarnation.

GC condemn captures the body token and writes condemned meta, spare CASes condemned to clean, and delete removes the body by exact token before deleting the meta; there is no tombstone handshake in v3.
The read path remains a body GET by content key at a constant blob_header_len offset and never consults .meta.
The raw-body v1 cut was rejected because dropping the in-body incarnation tag fixed the body etag to content and removed the protection that makes exact-token deletion miss a resurrected body.
The v2 terminal-tombstone design was superseded because it couples writer progress to GC and is unnecessary when the body tag changes the etag on resurrection.
Per-incarnation body keys were rejected because they require generation resolution by LIST, propagate incarnation into manifests, and break the pure-content/FUSE-ready design.
Phase A deletes tokened per-leaf promote revalidation and retained sources but keeps one presence check for every non-tokened leaf, including a fail-closed no-dep arm.
Phase A removes the view_gate drain because monotone retire-view installs and persistent graduated entries make in-closure reads see the required entries without the drain.
Phase A removes the writer fence-round refresh only when its TLA+ newborn-shard gate confirms the redundancy; the GC-side fence_round remains.
The no-paranoid-mode decision rejects retaining deleted checks behind a configuration flag; detection remains with ca-fsck, soak assertions, and system.content_addressed_log.

Adoption of an existing incarnation requires a durable precommit closure, so the Phase A plan adds chassert(precommitted) to both observeAndAdmit overloads; fresh uploads before precommit remain watermark-protected.
The v3 meta design estimates three paid PUTs per steady-state blob lifetime, roughly 150 bytes of metadata per live blob, and about 10 dollars per million blobs on AWS request pricing.
Mass-DROP metadata operations must use a bounded parallel pool because one million sequential metadata CASes at about 20 ms each would take roughly 5.5 hours.

The formal Gate A positive model removes tokened revalidation, the view drain, and writer fence refresh while preserving invariants; order, adoption-check, and non-tokened presence-check sabotages must fail.
Phase A removes redundant writer freshness machinery while retaining the dedup-adoption gate, promote owner check, and one non-tokened presence observation.
The reduced promote loop skips tokened leaves as edge-protected, but checks every non-tokened leaf for presence and fails closed on absent or condemned no-dep leaves.
A condemned non-tokened leaf is copy-forwarded only when isCopyForwardableTokenless is true; otherwise promote throws ABORTED.
The Phase A ordering guard treats dedup adoption before durable precommit as unsafe because an adopted blob carries the original writer's build_id and is not covered by the newborn-debris watermark.
Phase A migrates tokened promote tests from source resurrection to success with the token unchanged, while retaining the abandoned-precommit owner-check abort and tokenless/no-dep fail-closed tests.
The Phase A plan deletes the copy-forward pre-pass and accepts the rare in-closure GET+PUT because the in-closure gate is idempotent under CAS retry.
Freshness-meta v3 replaces writer-side RetireView retired-list downloads with per-hash .meta point-reads while leaving the exact-token body-delete core and read path unchanged.
The final BlobMeta shape is version, state in {clean, condemned}, condemn_round, and size; Tombstone and the incarnation nonce are excluded because metadata is not the delete linearizer.
Meta codec decoding fails closed on bad magic, version, length, or an invalid state value.
CAS pool layout changes from v3 metadata are handled by recreating development pools; there is no migration, compatibility scaffolding, dual read path, or configuration flag.
ca-inspect must dispatch .meta keys before the blobs/ body branch, and ca-fsck reports meta_without_body as an invariant violation while body_without_meta is benign pre-birth debris.

The writer point-reads metadata for condemned status, writes clean metadata after fresh body upload or resurrection, and may best-effort create clean metadata when adopting a present body with absent metadata.
Promote K3 point-reads metadata for non-tokened leaves; absent bodies still abort, condemned copy-forwardable leaves are copied forward, and tokened leaves remain skipped under EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE.
GC writes condemned metadata at condemn, clears it at spare, deletes it after exact-token body deletion, and performs per-hash metadata operations on a bounded parallel pool.
Graduation is re-keyed from condemn_round < min_ack to condemn_round < current_round, with min_ack removed from the GC fold interface.
The writer-side RetireView, syncer, observed_gc_round, and ack-floor are deleted only after all writer metadata point-read sites replace RetireView reads.

Freshness-meta validation requires CAS gtests, a deterministic GC-delete-versus-writer-resurrect race test, ASan, a CA-s3 lane with zero promote aborts and zero fsck dangles, and a soak with meta_without_body equal to zero.
